newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG STAY TOP AS RIVALS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG STAY TOP AS RIVALS DRAW.

text.p: Paris St Germain retained their lead without playing in the French soccer league after main rivals Bastia and Bordeaux were forced to settle for draws on Saturday.

With the Parisians travelling to Guingamp on Sunday, the focus was on Bordeaux and their star striker Jean-Pierre Papin, who returned to play in Marseille for the first time since he left the Mediterranean port four years ago.
Papin, who scored 180 goals for the former European champions in his six years in Marseille, was far less impressive on Saturday, the tie ending in a goalless draw.
The only satisfaction for Papin was that Bordeaux remained unbeaten after nine league matches.
With PSG firmly in command on 20 points, Bastia retained second place, two points adrift of the leaders, thanks to a 2-2 draw in an eventful game at bottom-of-the-table Nancy.

Nancy opened the scoring as early as the first minute through Ireland's Phil Gray but Bastia, who had a rare chance to go top for the first time in years, levelled thanks to Anton Drobnjak with an 18th minute penalty.
The Yugoslav, leading scorer in the league with eight goals, later missed another penalty, stopped by Nancy's keeper Frederic Roux, who was playing his first match in the first division.

In the meantime, Eric Rabesandratana had made it two for Nancy with yet another penalty in the 36th minute after Bastia lost Scot Jamie Fullarton, who received a red card after fisticuffs on the pitch.
But Bastia's Slovak playmaker Lubomir Moravcik equalised with a header 14 minutes from the end of the match.
Other title contenders also failed to win. Monaco could do no better than a 1-1 home draw with Metz and champions Auxerre drew 0-0 away to Montpellier.
